name: IndexSignal – SEO Index Monitor for Google
author: fastindexing

sections.description:
Google indexing status in WordPress, without guesswork

IndexSignal is a Google indexing checker and SEO index monitor for WordPress and WooCommerce. From wp-admin, you can see which public posts, pages, and products are detected as indexed, which URLs have technical blockers, which have not been checked, and what action is available next.

IndexSignal focuses on the gap between publishing a WordPress page and seeing it in Google Search. It complements your existing on-page SEO plugin: IndexSignal does not rewrite titles, descriptions, schema, or sitemap settings.

Try the free URL index checker | Explore WordPress indexing with IndexSignal | Learn how Google indexing works | View pricing | Get help

What IndexSignal helps you do

  • Check available Google index-status evidence for WordPress posts, pages, WooCommerce products, and product categories.
  • Find pages missing from search without sorting through one long, unfiltered URL list.
  • Review observable indexability signals such as robots directives, canonical URLs, HTTP status, redirects, and sitemap discovery.
  • Separate URLs that appear indexed, need a current check, are ready for indexing, or should be fixed first.
  • Start an eligible URL indexing workflow only after reviewing the exact credit cost.
  • Monitor saved status evidence at D0, D5, D7, D10, and D14.
  • Work from the IndexSignal overview, Posts, Pages, Products, Gutenberg, the Classic Editor, bulk actions, or the WordPress admin bar.

Private local scan before connection

IndexSignal first discovers public WordPress content and local indexability signals on your own site. No account is required for this local scan, and nothing is sent to FastIndexing.io until an administrator chooses to connect for online checks.

The scanner supports posts, pages, WooCommerce products and categories, and same-host multilingual sitemap URLs. Private, password-protected, noindex, non-canonical, and catalog-hidden content is identified before an indexing workflow can start.

Free start and transparent credit control

  • One-time first-site allowance for up to 200 initial URL checks.
  • Separate 200-credit trial indexing balance at signup.
  • No credit is spent before you review and confirm an online action.
  • Current prices, excluded URLs, and any balance shortfall are shown before a workflow starts.
  • Google Search Console is optional.

Local discovery remains available without a connected account. Online checks, indexing workflows, monitoring, reports, notifications, and payments use the FastIndexing.io hosted service.

How it works

  1. Run the private local scan from IndexSignal in wp-admin.
  2. Review your WordPress URLs and any local indexing blockers.
  3. Connect an existing account or create a free account when you want an online check.
  4. Select URLs, review the live estimate, and explicitly confirm the action.
  5. Follow saved results and monitoring history without leaving WordPress.

Privacy and external services

IndexSignal is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.

After an administrator explicitly connects the plugin, IndexSignal sends the verified site URL, selected public URLs, local indexability signals, plugin version, and requested actions to the FastIndexing.io API. FastIndexing.io uses this data to provide remote URL checks, indexing workflows, monitoring, reports, billing, and support. Read the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service.

Optional Google authorization takes place in the hosted service. Google credentials, account passwords, and Google access tokens are never stored in WordPress. Stripe processes checkout and payment details outside WordPress.

Need help? Visit FastIndexing Help, use the contact form, or email support@fastindexing.io.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, open Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  2. Search for “IndexSignal” and select Install Now.
  3. Activate IndexSignal on one WordPress site.
  4. Open IndexSignal in wp-admin and run the private local site scan.
  5. Connect only when you are ready to run online checks or indexing workflows.

For a manual installation, upload the indexsignal-seo-index-monitor-for-google directory to /wp-content/plugins/, then activate the plugin.

IndexSignal supports WordPress multisite through separate activation and connection on each subsite. Network Activate is not supported.
sections.faq:
How do I check whether a WordPress page is indexed by Google?

Open IndexSignal, choose the page, and run Check index status. The saved result appears in the overview, the Pages and Indexing screen, and supported WordPress content screens. Google Search Console remains the authoritative source when it is connected; other available checks are shown as detected evidence, not a guarantee.

Why is my WordPress page not indexed?

Common causes include a noindex directive, a canonical URL pointing elsewhere, robots restrictions, redirects or errors, missing discovery signals, duplicate content, or content Google does not choose to retain. IndexSignal reports observable technical signals and separates pages that should be fixed before any indexing workflow is considered.

Is IndexSignal a replacement for an on-page SEO plugin?

No. On-page SEO plugins manage titles, descriptions, schema, sitemaps, and related settings. IndexSignal focuses on URL discovery, technical indexability, index-status checks, eligible indexing workflows, and saved monitoring history. They can be used together.

Does IndexSignal automatically submit every new post?

No. IndexSignal never starts a paid check or indexing workflow just because a post is published. You choose the URLs, see the exact cost, and confirm before anything starts.

Is Google Search Console required?

No. Google Search Console is optional. Available checks and workflows can be used without storing Google credentials in WordPress.

Does the plugin store my Google token?

No. Optional Google authorization and tokens stay in the hosted service infrastructure. WordPress stores only a revocable installation token for the connected site.

Does IndexSignal work with WooCommerce?

Yes. The local inventory includes public WooCommerce products and product categories. Out-of-stock status is informational; private, catalog-hidden, noindex, or non-canonical states may block or warn.

Does IndexSignal guarantee Google indexing?

No. Google makes every indexing decision. IndexSignal checks technical eligibility, starts only the workflow you confirm, monitors saved evidence, and applies Credit-Back or Money-Back terms only where they are explicitly shown before confirmation.

What happens when I disconnect?

The installation token is revoked on the hosted service and removed from WordPress. The local site scan is preserved unless you choose to remove local plugin data. Account billing records and remote reports remain subject to the account controls and retention policy.
sections.changelog:
0.1.4

  • Rebuild the WordPress.org listing around clear Google indexing, index-status, WordPress, and WooCommerce use cases.
  • Add direct documentation, checker, pricing, privacy, terms, and support links.
  • Remove infrastructure-provider terms from public marketing copy and clarify external-service boundaries.
  • Remove local credentials unconditionally during uninstall and bound remote installation revocation to five seconds.

0.1.3

  • Add complete German (de_DE) localization and make the Gutenberg sidebar strings translatable.
  • Refresh the WordPress.org banner and animated plugin icon for a clearer directory presentation.
  • Polish public copy, onboarding terminology, and the IndexSignal brand label.

0.1.2

  • Rename the WordPress plugin to IndexSignal and align the package, text domain, directory artwork, and documentation with the reserved WordPress.org permalink.
  • Preserve existing local settings, connection tokens, capabilities, and API protocol identifiers during the display-name migration.
